minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 18, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:06
p.m., on October 18, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 15, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:11 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:24 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

RECESS

At the hour of 5:08 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  October 18, 2010
 PRESENTATIONS

Items P1 and P2 were taken out of order.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers, for their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Francine Jones for volunteer
  hours with Mission Viejo Animal Services; (2) Barbara Wehrmann for volunteer hours at
  the Mission Viejo Library; (3) Craig Collings for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo
  Library; (4) Helen Reta for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and
  Senior Center; and (5) Pat Pene for volunteer hours with the Senior Community Activity
  Team (SCAT).

P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winner

  Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented the award to John and Valerie Green,
  owners of Oggi’s Pizza and Brewing Company.

P3.  Proclaim October 24, 2010, To Be World Polio Day in Mission Viejo

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Jim Hansen, Mission Viejo Rotary Club
  President.

P4.  Proclaim October 17 through October 23, 2010 To Be Friends of Libraries Week

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Beth McConaughy, President of the Friends
  of the Mission Viejo Library Board of Directors.

P5.  Update on the 22nd Annual Walk Against Drugs/Disaster Preparedness Expo

  The City Council received the presentation from Tammy Descoteaux, Crime Prevention
  Specialist.

P6.  National Character Education Conference/Youth Subcommittee Video Presentation

  The City Council received the video presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that she was very upset to learn that a City Council candidate
was struck by a vehicle while he was out placing campaign signs and she opposes the practice of
one candidate placing signs in front of another candidate’s signs.

Judy Iannaccone and George Avila, O.C. Human Relations, Santa Ana: presented the O.C.

City Council Minutes  2  October 18, 2010
 Human Relations Annual Report and discussed different ways that their organization has helped
Mission Viejo residents.

Jamie Stahle, M.V.: stated that traffic is unsafe on Via San Gabriel and the residents would like
speed humps to help regulate traffic speed.

Nathan DeLuca, M.V.: noted that Via San Gabriel is not safe for the residents and their children.
He asked the city to help by installing speed humps on their street.

Stephanie Ireys, M.V.: stated that children cannot play on the street and will never be able to
walk to school with the current traffic concerns. She expressed support for speed humps on Via
San Gabriel.

David Durrell, M.V.: discussed the many near accidents on Via San Gabriel and requested speed
humps to slow traffic for the safety of the children.

Donna Bourassa, Treasurer of the Mission Viejo Environmental Homeowners Association,
M.V.: complained that a City Council Candidate trespassed on her property and put his campaign
sign in her yard and on the HOA property without permission.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: stated that political sign activity has gotten out of control and a specific
group of people act like they are above the law.

Dan Avery, M.V.: noted that Mission Viejo is a wonderful place to live and he thanked the City
Council for doing a great job.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: commended the City Council on the Community of Character Program.
She further stated that there are a lot of conclusions being drawn from limited information about
political activities. She feels people should be very careful about making accusations without all
of the facts.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3 and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

City Council Minutes  3  October 18, 2010
   Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 4, 2010, as
  presented.

4.  Check Register dated September 24, 2010, in the amount of $4,827,516.36

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated October 1, 2010, in the amount of $818,502.50

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for August 2010

  Received and filed.

7.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for August
  2010

  Received and filed.

8.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer's Monthly
  Report for August 2010

  Received and filed.

10.  Amendment to the Agreement for Temporary Contract Planner Services

  Authorized the City Manager to Approve a Contract Amendment with Lilley Planning
  Group to Increase the Amount of the Contract by $40,000, for a Total of $70,000, and
  Extend the Term of the Contract Through June 30, 2011.

11.  Confirmation of E-Verify Procedures

  Adopted Resolution 10-56 Confirming the E-Verify Audit Process.

12.  Number not used

13.  Bleacher Shade Covers Project (CIP 321) - Notice of Completion

City Council Minutes  4  October 18, 2010
   (1) Authorized the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days
  respectively after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City; and (2) authorized the payment of the final
  retention of $10,680.80 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

14.  Outdoor Fitness Equipment for Public Use at Oso Viejo Park - Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Authorized the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days
  respectively after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City; and (2) authorized the payment of the final
  retention of $6,203.20 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register dated September 17, 2010, in the amount of $1,005,817.93

  Council Member Schlicht drew attention to item #3 on page 4. She noted that there is a
  Turf Lane Park charge for C&D Electric in the amount of $2,027.28 that was not listed in
  the recent Turf Lane update provided to the City Council. She stated that including this
  charge, the City is 22% over budget on the Turf Lane Park rehabilitation project.

  Mr. Wilberg reiterated that $80,000 was an estimate included in the agreement and on
  several occasions he told the City Council that the project would exceed that.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Proposed Consent to Transfer and Sale of the Arroyo Vista Affordable Housing
  Project to Eden Arroyo Vista Associates, L.P. pursuant to the Affordable Housing

City Council Minutes  5  October 18, 2010
   Agreement between the CDA and Arroyo Vista Associates; Approval of Assignment
  and Assumption and Consent Agreement

  Celeste Brady, Community Development Agency Special Counsel, presented the staff
  report.

  Terese McNamee, Chief Finanical Officer for Eden Housing, answered questions of the
  City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  adopt CDA Resolution 10-09 Approving the Transfer and Sale of the Arroyo Vista
  Affordable Housing Project and All Interests Therein to Eden Arroyo Vista Associates,
  L.P. Pursuant to That Certain Affordable Housing Agreement Between the Agency and
  Arroyo Vista Associates, as Participant; Approving the Assignment and Assumption
  Agreement and Agency Consent Among Said Parties; and Making Certain Findings and
  Authorizations In Connection Therewith.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

16.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

17.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

18.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Council Minutes  6  October 18, 2010
 Referring to the presentations earlier in the evening, City Manager Wilberg thanked the many
volunteers for their support. He noted that volunteers provide a valuable service and make
significant contributions to the city of Mission Viejo.

Council Member Schlicht stated that she doesn't remember the Council giving the City Manager
authority to go beyond $80,000 for the Turf Lane Park rehabilitation.

Mr. Wilberg reminded the Council that he brought the matter up at the August 2010 City Council
Meeting. At that time, he specifically advised the Council that the project would exceed the
$80,000 estimate and he asked the Council for direction that evening if they wished for staff to
stop the project at $80,000. He noted that the Council's direction was to complete the park up to
$110,000.

Council Member Schlicht stated that the City Manager did not have the moral or legal authority
to spend beyond $80,000 but it was obvious the Council majority was not going to stop him and
she doesn't understand how the city can come to a legal agreement and then just blow it off.

City Attorney’s Report

19.  City Council and Administrative Authority: Hierarchy of Municipal Regulatory
  Enactments

  City Attorney Bill Curley indicated that Council Member Schlicht had asked if he would
  put together a report discussing the difference between an ordinance and a policy and
  therefore the report was provided with this agenda item.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma stated that he looks forward to seeing the city’s residents at the 22nd
Annual Walk Against Drugs, Saturday morning.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she met with several citizen groups over the last two
weeks and she discussed her attendance at a recent Diablos football game as the team took
another victory. She noted that the Capistrano Unified School District has teamed up with the
District Attorney to create a Gang Reduction and Intervention Program (GRIP). As part of the

City Council Minutes  7  October 18, 2010
 program, students at Newhart Middle School will be greeted by parents wearing orange vests
who are there to make sure students are abiding by the school dress code. Council Member
Schlicht also announced that she is looking forward to the Walk Against Drugs on Saturday and
she reminded residents that there will be an AlertOC emergency notification test on October 21,
2010. She advised residents to sign up for this reverse 911 program if they have not already
done so. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments by reminding residents that
elections are paramount because of conditions at the local, state, and national levels and it is
imperative that voters study the candidates.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury echoed his colleague’s comments regarding the Walk Against Drugs and
stated that he is looking forward to the event on Saturday.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness reminded residents that the Walk Against Drugs/Emergency
Preparedness Expo will be held on Saturday, October 23, 2010, and he invited residents to come
to this great event.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley restated that the Walk Against Drugs begins at 8:00 a.m. on Saturday, October 23
at Mission Viejo High School. She encouraged residents to arrive early in order to get a free t-
shirt and to find a seat in the high school stadium. After the presentations, participants will walk
from Mission Viejo High School to Oso Viejo Park for the Disaster Preparedness Expo and Fair.
The Drug Walk is the culmination of a year’s worth of planning, the hard work of Police
Services staff, and the event is always a community highlight. Mayor Kelley noted that she and
Mayor Pro Tem Leckness attended two senior transportation meetings this past week at Casta del
Sol and at the Murray Community and Senior Center. They concluded that there are a multitude
of offerings but the information can be very complicated. She encouraged residents to contact
her, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, or a city staff member for more information on all of the
programs available to seniors. She also reminded residents to reserve November 11, 2010, for
the Veteran’s Day Ceremony. The commanding officer of the city’s adopted Marine Battalion
will be the guest speaker and the Orange County Fire Authority Pipes and Drums will provide
the music. Mayor Kelley outlined her attendance at several recent events including Walk to
School Day with Bathgate Elementary students and the Linda Vista Elementary School carnival.
She also discussed the Orange County Triathlon which was held on October 10 and she
encouraged residents to watch for information on the triathlon and plan to attend next year.
Mayor Kelley announced that she is making businesses visits within the city and she recently
discovered the wonderful Mission Ranch Market on Los Alisos Boulevard. They have all the
offerings of a full grocery store and a restaurant with many different food items. She encouraged
residents to visit the market and to do their best to support Mission Viejo businesses. Finally,
Mayor Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of October is
respect.

City Council Minutes  8  October 18, 2010
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:10 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Joan Frances Knaggs, to Monday,
November 1, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 1, 2010

City Council Minutes  9  October 18, 2010
